prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” lawyer for every car-wreck case — the right lawyer depends on your case details and priorities (severity of injuries, who was at fault, whether the insurer disputes liability, whether you want to go to trial, budget, etc.). I can help you find the best fit. A few quick questions first:

- Where in Houston (ZIP or neighborhood)?  
- How serious are the injuries/property damage?  
- Was anyone at fault disputed? Was the police report filed?  
- Do you already have an attorney or are you looking for one now?

While you decide, here are practical steps and criteria to use when choosing a Houston personal injury lawyer:

What to look for
- Relevant experience: substantial motor-vehicle/catastrophic-injury experience in Texas courts.  
- Trial experience and a proven settlement record (many cases settle, but you want an attorney who will try the case if necessary).  
- Board certification in Personal Injury Trial Law (if present) or other recognitions (Super Lawyers, AV Preeminent by Martindale-Hubbell).  
- Good client reviews and clear communication.  
- Contingency-fee agreement (common: 33–40% if they handle the claim).  
- No disciplinary actions (check Texas State Bar records).  
- Resources to handle medical bills, experts, and litigation costs.

Where to search and verify
- Texas State Bar “Find a Lawyer” and disciplinary records.  
- Super Lawyers and Martindale-Hubbell ratings.  
- Google and Yelp for client reviews.  
- Local referrals from friends, doctors, or other lawyers.

Questions to ask during a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases like mine have you handled?  
- What percentage of your cases go to trial? What were typical settlement ranges?  
- Who in the firm will handle my case day-to-day?  
- What is your fee structure and any additional costs?  
- How will you communicate updates and how often?  
- Do you have references from past clients?

Time-sensitive items
- Texas statute of limitations for most car-accident injury claims: 2 years from the crash date (so act promptly).  
- Seek medical attention and document injuries, keep photos, medical bills, police report, and witness info.

If you want, I can:
- Provide a shortlist of highly rated Houston personal-injury attorneys/firms near you (I’ll need your ZIP or neighborhood), or  
- Draft an email or list of questions you can use when contacting attorneys.

Which option would you prefer?
